description: Kioku's dependency bot. `03-technical-design.md` §13.5: a bot has nothing to read until a manifest exists, so it arrives with the first one rather than afterwards. Two ecosystems — npm at the root, and PEP 621 under worker/ since #3 (its `pep621` manager matches `pyproject.toml` where it sits and maintains `uv.lock`, so no rule was needed) — and one config, because both flows answer to the same six pins.

packageRules.description: PIN 1/6 — psycopg[binary] >= 3.2.4. The floor is the lost-notification fix (`03` §3.1), not a number: below it, a notification can be dropped between LISTEN and the first poll. Bumping up is routine; going below it is never a cleanup. Arrived with #7, 2026-09-11: `worker/pyproject.toml` carries the same floor and `worker/loop.py` is the code it protects.

PIN 2/6 — SudachiDict-core 20260723. DO NOT BUMP. The dictionary version is part of the ingestion cache key, and an upgrade can change the identity of existing *notes* (`03` §5.3, ADR 0006). It is a deliberate, reviewed data event with a re-ingestion plan, never an automated bump. Arrives with #8.

PIN 3/6 — Nuxt 4.5.2, and @nuxt/kit lockstep with it. DO NOT BUMP. `noScripts`' behaviour under the Vercel preset was verified against this exact version (verification §8) and the rendering split is the reason Nuxt was chosen at all (ADR 0020). Nuxt 5 is scheduled for Q4 2026 and re-opens that question rather than inheriting the answer. @nuxt/kit rides along because `test/unit/nuxt-config.test.ts` reads nuxt.config through its loadNuxtConfig(): a kit on a different minor resolves a different Nuxt's defaults, and the guard would then be checking the wrong framework's config.

PIN 3/6, second half — nitropack ^2.13.4. The route rule is applied at render time inside the handler the Vercel preset packages verbatim (verification §8), and that was read at 2.13.4. Nitro 3 is a different renderer; it is a review, not a bump.

PIN 4/6 — ts-fsrs 5.4.2. 6.0.0 removes `elapsed_days` (verification §1.2). `04` builds no column on it so the major is survivable, but it is a data review rather than a version bump. Arrives with #12.

PIN 5/6 — drizzle-orm 0.45.2 is a SECURITY FLOOR, not a preference: the version exists because of a SQL-injection fix in sql.identifier() / sql.as() (`03` §13.2). It is also what builds both test databases — 0.45.2 exports ./pglite/migrator alongside ./node-postgres/migrator (ADR 0038), which is what stops the test schema forking from `04`. Below this version the ORM's own protection is what regresses. Arrives with #4.

PIN 6/6 — @electric-sql/pglite 0.5.8. DO NOT BUMP, and this pin has a second half that lives outside any manifest: the Postgres image tag beside it. `04` defaults every primary key to uuidv7(), a Postgres 18 built-in, so a PGlite that regressed to 17 fails on the first CREATE TABLE. PGlite does not document which PostgreSQL it builds — 0.5.8 = PostgreSQL 18.3 was measured (ADR 0038, verification §14.1). Nothing will tell you when the two halves diverge except a uuidv7() that stops existing, so both halves are asserted instead: test/schema/schema.test.ts for PGlite and worker/tests/conftest.py's POSTGRES_IMAGE for the container (#4 and #7).
Everything else: group the devDependencies so the weekly check is one PR to read rather than nine.
